notes.quota: V15-1 (architect design, 2026-09-25): reserved-and-settled TOKEN accounting, enforced by the Hermes runtime (patch 0010) for every model request of one run (main, every retry and reconnect, auxiliary, gateway and reviewer calls). Before each physical request the runtime reserves reservation_tokens (the served window, vLLM --max-model-len, prompt plus output: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/configuration/engine_args/); after a valid terminal response it settles to the reported usage; missing usage keeps the full reservation, an uncertain request keeps it until it can no longer be charged. A request is admitted while settled + open reservations + reservation_tokens <= token_allowance_per_window. No request ceiling. Admission (run-preflight.sh MODEL_RATE_BUDGET): sum of the allowances of every running migration run + reserve_tokens_per_window <= the MaaSSubscription limit: 51000000 + 9000000 = 60000000 for qwen3-8-27b-int4, 11000000 + 9000000 = 20000000 for qwen3-6-27b. Replaces the 190 requests/h ceiling, which charged every request at the full window and stalled v15 after 34 minutes (about 59K tokens per request measured). max_output_tokens is the largest output any request may ask for. max_wait_seconds bounds a worker's wait; beyond it the card is deferred neutrally (patch 0009).
notes.request_body: Both models explicitly disable thinking and pin their model card's non-thinking sampling in each request: Qwen3.8 temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8, top_k 20, min_p 0.0, presence_penalty 1.5, repetition_penalty 1.0 (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B#best-practices); Qwen3.6 the same values, its card's Instruct/Non-Thinking set (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B; E-1, 2026-10-01: the qwen3-6-27b server override is the card's thinking/precise-coding set 0.6/0.95/20/0/0.0/1.0, which does not apply to a worker that runs thinking off). Explicit per-run values prevent a server-default change from changing a run's sampling; the served defaults are unchanged for Kilo/OpenCode. A thinking-mode experiment must explicitly supply its own mode and sampling. v12 (2026-09-24, t_655b1607) ran two responses to the full output cap without the thinking-off row.
notes.source: B4: the ONE declared runtime profile per model and mode. dest-init generates every model-dependent worker setting from it (provider, caps, request body on the main slot and on every auto auxiliary slot, the request pacer); the migration-run provisioner pins a copy per run (<run>-run-control profile.json), and the loop refuses a runtime that differs from the pin.
notes.timeouts: vLLM buffers a tool call's arguments until complete; a ~12 KB file written through a tool call sends no bytes for ~4K tokens at ~18 tok/s, beyond Hermes's 120s default stream read timeout (pilot v5 M3 t_3efca989).
notes.compression: qwen3-6-27b only (E-1, v31, 2026-10-02): 7 of 57 implementer runs ended without a terminal call after 40-95 min at ~121-123K real prompt tokens against the 131072 window: HTTP 400 (prompt + 8192 output > window) after 3 compression attempts, or a >900 s prefill cut by the gateway. Compression at 0.80 x 110000 could not shrink a protected tail of 20 messages holding large tool results, and the no-LLM prune was off. The profile's block is merged over the base block: threshold_tokens fires compression at the lower of the ratio and this absolute count (Hermes docs), proactive_prune_tokens enables the tool-result prune (docs suggest 48000), protect_last_n keeps fewer raw messages. qwen3-8-27b-int4 deliberately carries NO block (decided 2026-10-02 with the Qwen 3.8 loop-trial owner): it keeps v30's base compression (0.80 x 220000, no prune, protect_last_n 20) -- the loop-escalation screen was measured on uncompressed v30 prompts (9 of 10 streak sessions had no compaction before the third-call note; at the note 3 of 9 prompts exceeded 72K and 7 of 9 exceeded 48K), v30 compacted in 2 of 48 sessions and never overflowed the 262144 window, a ~77K trigger is the v9 summary-timeout history behind the 0.80 ratio, and protect_last_n 12 is shorter than an 8-turn escalation (>= 16 messages). The A/B therefore runs each model in the configuration its window calls for, stated as such. run_scoped (qwen3-6-27b only; Hermes runtime patch 0021, v32 t_2a95f8c1 run 44): a card run is one turn, and the stock per-turn compaction budget (max_attempts 3) and insufficient-progress block switched compaction off after three passes that only pruned (the tail anchor kept the opening task message, so nothing was summarised); the real prompt then grew to 121,375 tokens and a request waited out the 900 s stale timeout. With run_scoped the runtime keeps compaction available for the whole run (a new pass after the projected request regrows by max(4096, 10% of the trigger)), keeps the opening task turn in the head so a pass summarises, follows a prune-only pass with a summarising one, and before every request compacts (or ends the run with context_ceiling_unreachable) when the projected prompt (last provider figure + 1.25 x the estimated addition) plus max_tokens exceeds context_length. qwen3-8-27b-int4 keeps the stock compaction (no compression block); the request ceiling (patch 0021) applies to both profiles from their own context_length and max_tokens.
notes.loop_escalation: qwen3-8-27b-int4 only (Hermes runtime patch 0017): after the guard's third identical-call note the worker's requests switch to this thinking bundle until the first edit (write_file/patch, or terminal sed -i, > src/, tee src/) or verification call (run-verify.sh, advance.py), or max_turns thinking turns (8, a judgement), then return to request_body. Evidence: tmp/v30-screen (v30 real prefixes on the INT4 pod: served profile repeated the command 25/27, thinking 0/27; at max_tokens 8192 xhigh ended in a tool call 14/15, medium 12/15). reasoning_effort travels inside chat_template_kwargs (vLLM 0.18's API field accepts none/low/medium/high only). reasoning_echo keeps the thinking turn's reasoning in the next turn. Ordinary-turn sampling is unchanged; never raise presence/repetition penalties or set frequency_penalty (tested: no cross-turn effect in vLLM 0.18). Patch 0018 adds two start triggers and a restart bound (absent keys = identical-call note only, unbounded): same_result_count 3 = that many consecutive near-duplicate calls to one tool (patch 0014's similarity) returning a byte-identical result (patch 0015's reading of a result), the v32 t_2f2509aa tail -c loop; same_call_count 5 = that many consecutive calls with identical arguments whatever the results, the v32 t_449a35e4 ls|wc -l;date;ps poll; repeat_read_count 3 within repeat_read_window 8 = that many of the last 8 calls each exactly repeat an earlier call (same tool and arguments, byte-identical result) with no edit in between, the v32 t_56432803 run 43 cycle over five brief sections; pollers exempt from the identical-call note are not counted, an edit, verification or typed-repair call restarts every count (and the repeat history), and a start on any of them appends a factual note to the triggering result. max_starts_per_signature 2 = one stall signature (tool plus argument hash, tool plus result hash, or for repeat-read one signature per no-edit stretch, which only an edit or a typed-repair run ends) starts at most 2 escalations in a run; the third start is a guardrail halt (loop_escalation_restart_halt). The worker's agent.log start line carries trigger=identical|same-result|same-call|repeat-read. Running the card's typed-repair.py also ends an escalation (end reason=typed-repair; v32 t_6d0f2b9f) and restarts both counts. retry_start_turns (v32 item 2): a retry whose card's PREVIOUS run ended in a loop halt (STOP WORKER_TOOL_LOOP), iteration exhaustion or RUN_TOKEN_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED starts on the thinking bundle for its first retry_start_turns turns: the harness launch shim (.hermes/kernel/worker_launch.py, HERMES_BIN) sets HERMES_START_ESCALATED_TURNS for that worker only; 8 matches max_turns.
notes.run_input_token_budget: v32 (2026-10-03): the shape-independent bound on ONE kanban worker run, in prompt tokens (sessions input+cache_read+cache_write of the run's session tree), enforced in the workspace by .hermes/kernel/run_budget.py (pre_tool_call): crossing it ends the run as RUN_TOKEN_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED through the same native call as an exhausted iteration budget (timed_out, counted toward max_retries). Before it the only such bound was the 500-iteration budget, which let one M1 run read 62.8M and one repository card ~46M input tokens; healthy Qwen 3.8 card runs read 0.3M-6M. 12000000 is twice the largest healthy run, a judgement. qwen3-6-27b pins the same number: its 72000-token compression trigger keeps each request smaller, so the same budget admits at least as many requests. Preflight refuses a selected profile without it.
